title: Culturing the Endocrine Junctional Zone of Mouse Placenta in Serum-Free Medium
author: Yung, Burton, et al.
materials: C57BL/6 mice, wild-type, pregnant at E12.5

steps.title: Generate timed pregnant mice
steps.instruction: Pair 10–16 week old male and virgin female mice, check each morning for a vaginal plug; the day a plug is observed is defined as embryonic day 0.5 (E0.5). Separate the plugged female from the male and house for an additional 12 days to reach embryonic day 12.5 (E12.5).

steps.title: Prepare reagents and Jz‑medium
steps.instruction: Autoclave phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS). Prepare the defined junctional‑zone (Jz) explant medium (Jz‑medium). Prepare 70 % ethanol for disinfection spray. Autoclave dissecting instruments and glassware or use sterile plasticware.

steps.title: Euthanize mouse and expose uterus
steps.instruction: Cervically dislocate the pregnant mouse. Sterilize the abdomen with 70 % ethanol and blot dry. Make a skin incision with blunt scissors and peel back the skin. Using a new pair of blunt scissors and blunt forceps, open the abdominal cavity.

steps.title: Remove uterus and keep on ice
steps.instruction: Excise the whole uterus and immediately submerge it in 50 mL ice‑cold PBS per animal in a Gosselin container; keep the container on ice and transport to a Class I MSC bench.

steps.title: Isolate individual implantation sites
steps.instruction: Place the uterus in a 100 mm dish with ice‑cold PBS, rinse briefly, then grasp the junction between the two uterine horns and lift them out of the PBS. Using fine scissors, cut between each implantation to separate them. Transfer each implantation to a separate 35 mm dish containing ice‑cold PBS, cover the dish, and keep on ice.

steps.title: Remove decidua and amniotic sac
steps.instruction: Under a stereo‑microscope, use fine forceps to remove remaining uterine tissue surrounding the amniotic sac and placenta. Peel the decidua layer from the basal (outer convex) surface of the placenta, starting at the edge and progressing toward the centre. After the decidua is removed, separate the amniotic sac from the placenta and cut the umbilical cord as close as possible to the chorionic plate.

steps.title: Separate labyrinth from junctional zone
steps.instruction: Lay the placenta flat with the chorionic surface (umbilical cord attached) facing upward. Identify the central red labyrinth and the paler rim (junctional zone). Using two forceps, gently hold the placenta and tease apart the labyrinth by inserting closed forceps at the boundary and slowly opening them around the disc. Flip the placenta, lift the edge of the junctional zone, and continue teasing the two layers apart toward the centre until fully separated. Remove any residual pink labyrinth tissue from the junctional zone.

steps.title: Dice junctional zone into cubes
steps.instruction: Transfer the isolated junctional zone to a dish containing pre‑cooled DMEM/F12 (Jz‑medium). Using fine forceps under the stereo‑microscope, dice the tissue into cubes of approximately 1–1.5 mm³. Place the diced tissue from one or two placentas into a 15 mm (or 24 mm) diameter Netwell™ insert.

substeps.instruction: If placentas are of the same genotype, the same dish of Jz‑medium may be reused; otherwise use clean forceps and a new insert for each placenta.
Clean forceps by dipping in 70 % ethanol followed by three sequential rinses in PBS.

steps.title: Set up explant cultures
steps.instruction: Transfer each Netwell™ insert containing junctional‑zone explants into a 12‑well plate (1 mL Jz‑medium per well) or a 6‑well plate (3 mL Jz‑medium per well). Ensure all explants are fully submerged under the medium.

steps.title: Incubate explants 48 h
steps.instruction: Place the plate in a humidified incubator set to 37 °C with 5 % CO₂ and 10 % O₂ (balance N₂) for 48 hours.

steps.title: Assess viability with MTT
steps.instruction: Add MTT stock (50 mg/mL) to each well to achieve a final concentration of 500 µg/mL. Incubate for 1 hour in the incubator. Dark blue/purple staining indicates viable tissue.

steps.title: Harvest explant tissue and snap‑freeze
steps.instruction: At the end of incubation, remove the junctional‑zone explants from the inserts, place each in a 1.5 mL tube, and snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen for downstream analyses (e.g., Western blot, PCR).

steps.title: Collect and clarify conditioned medium
steps.instruction: Collect the conditioned medium (CM) from each well, either separately or pooled into 15 mL or 50 mL centrifuge tubes. Centrifuge at 4000 rpm (1771 g) for 30 minutes at 4 °C to pellet debris. Transfer the clear supernatant to a new tube.

steps.title: Concentrate conditioned medium (optional)
steps.instruction: If concentration is required, load the clarified CM into a Vivaspin centrifugal concentrator and centrifuge according to the manufacturer’s instructions until the volume is reduced 20‑ to 30‑fold. Transfer the concentrated CM to a 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Store samples at –80 °C
steps.instruction: Store both the snap‑frozen junctional‑zone tissue fragments and the (concentrated) conditioned medium at –80 °C until further analysis.
